1 · Upload the document

Download carousel.pdf (56.5 MB, vector text) → LinkedIn → start a post → add a document → upload the PDF → title it: Priority, Not Permission

2 · Paste the post copy

66 data center pods. 330 to 350 turbines. 3.5 miles of cable. The federal notice never says how much seabed.

Nothing is being built on the floor of Cook Inlet.

FERC says the sole purpose of a preliminary permit is "priority to file a license application."
It authorizes no land-disturbing work and no entry onto lands or waters owned by others.
The notice doesn't say how deep the water is or how long the permit runs.
Alaska Energy Authority says it will file to intervene and oppose. It says it has had no communication with the applicant.

The record is one federal notice with three blanks in it, and one September 14th newspaper report quoting Curtis W. Thayer for the state.

Comments on FERC docket P-15423-000 close 5:00 p.m. Eastern on November 2nd. The window takes competing applications for the same site. Who does it serve more, objectors or a rival?

#CookInlet #FERC #TidalEnergy

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

READ THIS BEFORE YOU POST: it ships with a flagged shortfall. 7.98 clears the threshold that applies after four revision rounds, 7.70, and it does NOT clear the unrelaxed 8.3 the doctrine quotes. The scorer asked that the shortfall be named here rather than buried in a number, so: this is the fourth deck this month to ship below 8.3, it took four revision rounds against a house norm of two, and the weakest criterion is artwork craft at 7 on the deck’s heaviest weight. Its fix is already written down from No.60 and is the next deck’s work order, not this one’s. Two further things you should know. The PDF is 56.5 MB against the house band of 2 to 25, because shrink_pdfs.py refused every image at 41.4 dB against its 42.0 dB floor; it is under LinkedIn’s 100 MB document cap and will upload, but expect it to be slow, and the cause is this deck’s own high-frequency texture rather than a bug. The rubric’s ten criterion weights sum to 1.10, not 1.00, so the literal weighted sum is 8.78 and the normalised one is 7.98; the two readings disagree about whether a deck of straight sevens and eights should ever have to iterate. That is a maintainer call and it is written up in the run’s worklog with both repairs spelled out, because they are not equivalent.

Editor's note

The caption room's winner was candidate B, COLD NUMBER over PUNCH THEN PROOF, and it ships byte for byte. The caption-critic made one fix, replacing the deck summary line so it names the actual record, one federal notice with three blanks and one newspaper report quoting Curtis W. Thayer. The showrunner additionally added the docket number to the close, because the critic found that NEITHER candidate carried it while slide 09's single ask is a filing, and an ask to file that doesn't name the docket is an ask nobody can act on. The fact-checker killed nine claims, including the seabed acreage, the water depth and the four year permit term that were circulating in coverage, and three of those kills became the keepable frame at slide 06, where the absences are printed as voids rather than quietly dropped.

The live site, looked at today

Every published page and the Cook Inlet Gas Watch page are read once a run. A clean pass is reported for the same reason a failure is: silence is what a broken site would also produce.
SITE SIGN-OFFWARN, 119 pages, 18 checks, UNFIXED gaswatch.jsonl is current. 17 of 18 clean. The one warn is the Gas Watch staleness below, not a page fault: every page is on disk and substantial, 5,050 clickable links resolve, every asset is present, every sitemap entry has a page, and the videos passthrough is intact.
GAS WATCHGAS WATCH LIVE: FAIL on source freshness, DISCLOSED UPSTREAM, re-audited 2026-09-21T10:12Z. 13 of 14 checks PASS. CINGSA has published no reading since 2026-09-13T21:00 Alaska, 173.1 hours, because it is in its announced semiannual shut-in field balance and maintenance, September 14th to September 21st, with Compressor B down. Its dashboard answers HTTP 200 and carries that notice. THE COLLECTOR IS HEALTHY: gaswatch.yml ran and succeeded, the live dataset holds 48 daily records with no calendar gaps, and every day since the shut-in is recorded UNVERIFIED with no measurement carried forward. Recorded in runs/2026-09-21/gaswatch_incident.json, blocker upstream, five attempts, three evidence URLs. It is also why CI's checks job is red on this run's PR, which is explained there.
CRON HEALTHPASS, 6 scheduled workflows audited at 2026-09-21T07:15Z plus Pages and published output, no repairs needed.
SITE FIXESone, and it was a merge rather than a defect. main moved during Phase 12 when the Gas Watch collector appended 2026-09-21's record and rebuilt the gas watch page, which conflicted with this run's docs/ in seven generated files. Resolved by taking the base side and re-running site_build.py, never by hand-editing a build product; site_fresh_check confirms docs/ is exactly a fresh build, 208 generated files. Nothing on the live site was broken.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post Tuesday through Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time, which are the strongest slots for this audience.
  • This deck has a shelf life. Its single ask is a filing deadline of November 2nd, so post it well before that date or it reads as history.
  • Paste the source block as the FIRST comment within 60 seconds of posting, with the full raw URLs visible.
  • Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. Early replies are what turn a docket post into a conversation.
  • First correction to keep ready. Nothing is being built on the floor of Cook Inlet. A preliminary permit grants priority to file a license application, not permission to construct anything.
  • Second correction to keep ready. The Alaska Energy Authority STATED AN INTENTION to file to intervene and oppose, as of September 14th. The deck never says it has filed, and neither should a reply.
  • Check saves at 48 hours and log them. A save is worth about five times a like on this platform now, and slide 06 was built for exactly that.
